evaluation.note: Status metadata was added after measurement. Replacements are unchanged. Rejected at the predeclared bridge screen: display excess improves, but both detail guards fail. No production edit or six-view adoption evaluation.

hypothesis: V2-3l locates most facade residual energy at transitions or mixed support. The shipped 16-tap filter narrows the single-sample pane smoothing when it engages. Retaining that near path and matching its uncapped axis-aligned second moment with a centred, normalized, irregular 16-tap kernel may stabilize boundaries without an arbitrary dimming or global blur.

provenance.origin: V2-3h filter-width diagnosis and V2-3l pair-local support analysis
design: Change only the sixteen footprint offsets. Keep the single-sample emission, fade thresholds, per-sample AA, room occupancy and brightness factors unchanged.
Eight R2 points at indices 1 through 8 and their negatives give zero first moment. Whiten their covariance and scale it to 75/256 = 0.29296875 per axis; equal weights remain 1/16.

For an axis-aligned uncapped pane edge, the smoothstep derivative kernel with half-width a has variance a*a/5. Shipped single-sample a=1.25 pixels gives variance 0.3125; the microfilter a=0.3125 gives 0.01953125. Offsets supply their difference, 0.29296875.

This matches a second moment, not the full kernel. The 0.12 grid-unit clamp, skewed footprints, spatially varying centroid derivatives and the finite facade can invalidate that model. Positive normalized weights preserve a constant and phase-integrated brightness for a translation-invariant periodic signal; they do not guarantee the brightness of this rendered view.
provenance.acceptance: Unchanged V2-3g rule across all six views: display excess, measured noise or 1% tolerance, 4px/16px reference guards. Record mean HDR and display luminance as non-deciding diagnostics. No performance measurement.
